rationale: The inline link is underlined at rest but a:hover sets text-decoration:none, so in the hover state color (#1a73e8) is the ONLY differentiator from the body text. Color used as the sole visual means in that state fails 1.4.1 (F73); even though link-vs-body is 3.863:1, the G183 path requires the supplemental cue to be present in the hover state.
citation: "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color

rationale: Underlined at rest, but a:focus removes the underline (and outline:none), so keyboard-focused users see a color-only link. The supplemental cue must be available on focus per G183; here it is absent in the focus state, leaving color as the sole differentiator.
citation: "Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text and providing additional visual cues on focus for links or controls where color alone is used to identify them." — Technique G183

rationale: The inline link has no underline in any state and link-vs-body (#1a5fb4 vs #1a1a1a) is 2.768:1, below the 3:1 floor required by the G183 3:1+cue path. With no non-color cue and an insufficient color difference, it is not visually evident without color vision (F73).
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 1.4.1 due to creating links that are not visually evident without color vision." — Failure F73

rationale: At rest the link is underlined and blue (ok), but a:visited removes the underline AND sets the color to #222222, which is 1.094:1 against the body text #1a1a1a — effectively the same color. In the visited state there is no non-color cue and no color difference, so the link is indistinguishable. This is NOT merely a browser-setting color change because the visited rule ALSO removes the only non-color cue.
citation: "another visual, onscreen method is used to convey the information which does not use color." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: No underline in any state; the only thing :hover changes is the hue (#1a5fb4 to #0b5cad, 2.609:1 vs body). A color-to-color change is still color as the sole differentiator, so the link is not evident without color vision in any state (F73).
citation: "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information ... or distinguishing a visual element." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color

rationale: Link #1e63b0 vs body text #1a1a1a is 2.873:1 — just under the 3:1 floor — and there is no underline in any state. The G183 3:1+cue path is not satisfied (both the 3:1 differentiator and the supplemental cue are missing), so color is the only, and insufficient, differentiator (F73).
citation: "Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text and providing additional visual cues on focus ..." — Technique G183

rationale: At rest the non-color cue is bold (font-weight:700). a:focus drops to font-weight:400 with no underline and outline:none, so the keyboard-focused state is distinguished by color (#1a73e8) alone. The supplemental cue is not available in the focus state, so G183 is not met for that state.
citation: "providing additional visual cues on focus for links or controls where color alone is used to identify them." — Technique G183

rationale: There is no underline in any state, so even at rest the link relies on color only (#1a5fb4 vs body = 2.768:1, under 3:1). In the visited state the color becomes #222222 (1.094:1 vs body #1a1a1a), so the link is the same color as the surrounding text and has no cue at all — not evident without color vision (F73).
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 1.4.1 due to creating links that are not visually evident without color vision." — Failure F73

rationale: Underlined at rest, but BOTH a:hover and a:focus set text-decoration:none, so in either interactive state color (#0d6efd, 3.867:1 vs body) is the only differentiator. The supplemental cue must persist in the hover and focus states for the G183 path; it is removed in both.
citation: "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information ... or distinguishing a visual element." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color

rationale: The only non-color cue (an underline) appears solely on :hover. At rest and on keyboard :focus there is no underline, leaving color only (#1a5fb4 = 2.768:1 vs body, under 3:1). Per Trusted Tester 13.A a cue that appears only on mouse-over is not considered onscreen, so it cannot satisfy the requirement; the focus and rest states fail.
citation: "Alternate text that appears on mouse-over ... is not considered onscreen text." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: On :hover the underline is removed and an inline ::after mask-image SVG icon appears instead. Whether that icon is a meaningful, perceivable non-color cue or merely decoration cannot be determined from the DOM/CSS by a static analyzer, so the runner should abstain on whether the in-state cue is adequate. Labeled positive because if the icon does not read as a cue, the hover state is color-only.
citation: "another visual, onscreen method is used to convey the information which does not use color." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: On :hover the real text-decoration underline is removed and replaced by a repeating background-image stripe intended to look like an underline. Whether the image actually renders a perceivable underline (color, position, contrast) cannot be resolved from the DOM alone, so the runner should abstain. Labeled positive because if the image cue does not render perceivably, the hover state is color-only.
citation: "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information ... or distinguishing a visual element." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color

rationale: The underline (a non-color cue) is explicitly retained in rest, hover, focus, and visited states. Because a non-color differentiator is present in every state, the link is distinguishable without relying on color; passes 1.4.1.
citation: "another visual, onscreen method is used to convey the information which does not use color." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: At rest the link relies on color, but link-vs-body (#1a73e8 vs #1a1a1a) is 3.863:1 (>= 3:1) AND a supplemental underline appears on BOTH :hover and :focus. This is exactly the G183 3:1+cue-on-focus path, so the link is conformant.
citation: "Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text and providing additional visual cues on focus for links or controls where color alone is used to identify them." — Technique G183

rationale: The link is both bold (font-weight:700) and underlined in rest, hover, focus, and visited. Two non-color cues persist in every state, so the link is never distinguished by color alone; passes regardless of the color difference.
citation: "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information ... or distinguishing a visual element." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color

rationale: Belt-and-braces pass: link-vs-body (#0d6efd vs #1a1a1a) is 3.867:1 (>= 3:1) AND the underline persists in every state. It conforms by both the persistent-cue path and the G183 3:1 path.
citation: "Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text and providing additional visual cues on focus ..." — Technique G183

rationale: The underline (non-color cue) is present in rest, hover, focus, AND visited; the only thing :visited changes is the link color (to purple #6c2bd9). Per Trusted Tester 13.A a visited link changing color is a browser setting and is NOT failed for 13.A, and because the underline still distinguishes the link in the visited state, it passes 1.4.1.
citation: "It is considered a browser setting if a visited link changes color — this is not failed for 13.A." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: Bold (font-weight:700) is the non-color cue and persists in rest, hover, focus, and visited. Only the color changes on :visited (to #7b2fbe). A visited color change alone is a browser setting per TT 13.A (not a failure), and the bold cue still distinguishes the link in the visited state, so it passes 1.4.1.
citation: "It is considered a browser setting if a visited link changes color — this is not failed for 13.A." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: G183/F73's inline-link rule applies to links embedded in a block of text. This link is a standalone item in a <nav> list (flex row, padded list items, bottom border), not embedded mid-sentence, and is distinguished by layout/position rather than by color within running text — out of scope for the inline-link color-only failure, so it passes.
citation: "Failure of Success Criterion 1.4.1 due to creating links that are not visually evident without color vision." — Failure F73 (applies to links in a block of text)

rationale: Hover and focus darken the color (#1a73e8 to #0d47a1) but the underline is retained in rest, hover, and focus. Since a non-color cue is always present, the in-state color change does not make the link color-only; passes 1.4.1.
citation: "another visual, onscreen method is used to convey the information which does not use color." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: The non-color cue is a 2px dotted border-bottom (an underline-equivalent) that persists in rest, hover, focus, and visited. A non-color differentiator is present in every state, so the link is never color-only; passes 1.4.1.
citation: "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information ... or distinguishing a visual element." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color

rationale: Against a body text of #212121 the link #1a73e8 is 3.574:1 (>= 3:1) and an underline appears on BOTH :hover and :focus. The G183 3:1+cue-on-focus path is satisfied, so the link conforms.
citation: "Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text and providing additional visual cues on focus for links or controls where color alone is used to identify them." — Technique G183

rationale: The :visited state fades the color toward the body (#222222, 1.094:1 vs #1a1a1a) but KEEPS the underline. Even though the visited color cue weakens to nothing, the underline (a non-color cue) is still present in the visited state, so the link remains distinguishable without color; passes 1.4.1.
citation: "another visual, onscreen method is used to convey the information which does not use color." — Trusted Tester 5.1.3 (13.A)

rationale: Link #2563eb vs body #1a1a1a is 3.367:1 (>= 3:1), and the underline persists in rest, hover, focus, and visited. The link conforms by both the persistent non-color cue and the G183 3:1 differentiator.
citation: "Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text and providing additional visual cues on focus ..." — Technique G183
